comparator.academicYear: Current published three-year prospectus curriculum, checked 2026-09-25
comparator.sourceNotes: Year one has 60 EC of compulsory courses (15 historical, 35 systematic and 10 academic skills); two 0-EC induction/tests do not count. Year two comprises 30 EC compulsory philosophy and research, 15 EC chosen from three of four great-text courses, and 15 EC genuinely free electives. Year three comprises 10 EC compulsory study, five 5-EC seminars selected from eight (25 EC), a 15-EC open minor and a required 10-EC philosophical bachelor essay. This illustrative coherent path chooses the first three listed second-year great-text options and a balanced permitted selection of third-year seminars; seminar topics change yearly and the free space is not assigned invented content.

alternatives.concept: A broad philosophical curriculum combining ethics, metaphysics, free will, political thought and close reading with empirical study of perception, cognition and language. The empirical and literary courses deepen particular philosophical questions without replacing Radboud’s specialist philosophy seminars or required philosophical thesis. Political philosophy and social theory also connect questions about the self to civic life and rights.

alternatives.concept: An ethics and political philosophy curriculum that tests ideas about justice, authority, rights and responsibility against constitutional and EU institutions, environmental justice and conflict. It exchanges the first curriculum’s sustained cognitive-science and literary interpretation strands for public and social questions supported by Radboud’s social/political philosophy, humanities-in-practice and Planet and Politics components. Philosophy of mind and emotion remain as questions about moral agency.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Eight substantively motivated replacements remove the mind/neuroscience and literary-interpretation sequence and add comparative constitutional/EU institutions, international politics, governance and environmental justice. The second programme asks normative questions about public life rather than pursuing the first programme’s mind and knowledge emphasis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad first programme treats foundational philosophy through questions of mind, knowledge and human experience. The second changes eight courses and reorganises the evidence around ethics, politics, rights and public life. A third based on philosophical texts or reasoning is already integrated into both and would require unrelated substitutions for a distinct 24-course programme.

notes.text: Radboud provides a structured sequence in philosophy, specialist seminars and a required philosophical bachelor essay while preserving 30 EC of free choice. UCR studies several philosophical questions with cognition, politics and society, but has fewer specialist philosophy courses and no required philosophy thesis.
